newsitem.title: ITALY: OAU chief says U.S. has role to play over Zaire.
newsitem.headline: OAU chief says U.S. has role to play over Zaire.

text.p: The head of the Organisation of African Unity urged the United Nations on Thursday to back international intervention to save war refugees in Zaire and said Washington had an important role to play.

"The important thing right now, given the situation in the area, is how fast can a neutral force be deployed in Zaire," OAU Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim told Reuters in an interview after talks with Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini.
Salim said it was up to the Security Council to make a move.
"I am told the Security Council is scheduled to meet this afternoon and I would hope...they will be able to take a decision," he said.

France has pushed for a U.N. resolution authorising immediate intervention in eastern Zaire to protect more than a million starving Hutu refugees who have fled fighting between Tutsi-led rebels and the Zairean army.
Diplomats said earlier this week that Germany and Italy were drafting a resolution but the United States and Britain, which sit on the Security Council, appeared hesitant to intervene.

"The United States has an important role to play in this," Salim said. "It's true that the crisis came at a difficult time in the midst of presidential elections...but President Clinton has been re-elected."
An eight-nation African summit in Nairobi called on Tuesday for a neutral force to be deployed in eastern Zaire. Only France, Spain and Ethiopia have so far offered to commit troops.

French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette has accused the international community of "spinelessness" for failing to take action as concern grows that thousands of refugees will die while the world drags its feet.
The U.S. State Department said on Wednesday that Washington was leaning towards backing the proposed force logistically but would not commit ground troops.

Dini said Italy supported making whatever contribution was possible but added: "We want to wait for a request before taking any decision. We want to act in a co-ordinated fashion with other countries."

European Union aid ministers met in Brussels on Thursday to try to hammer out a joint approach, while U.N. officials quoted eyewitness accounts from the harsh mountains of eastern Zaire saying Rwandan refugees were literally dying of thirst.
Salim urged the rapid deployment of a neutral force. "The sooner it is done the better," he said.

"This is not one of those situations where one can afford the luxury of time. The longer the situation goes on this way, the more likelihood of people suffering and also the more likelihood of greater instability."

Salim said ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seke, who has been absent from his country since August receiving treatment for prostate cancer and is now in France, should return speedily. Mobutu has given his backing to the proposed international force.
"The presence of Mobutu in Zaire...would be a very major plus," Salim said.
